correctness.rationale: Independently exhausted all initial states at lengths 1–7 using disjoint excited and refractory bit planes, two rail shifts and a rung swap to compute the synchronous threshold-two update. The small maxima are 2,3,3,4,4,4,5. At time three there are no excitations on lengths ≤6, and on length 7 the only time-three sites are the two middle vertices (108 initial words in each case). Projecting the actual upper words onto single rungs gives exactly the seven frozen sets; the product of their cardinalities is the observed 108, establishing equality with the Cartesian product. Rail swap proves the lower identity, and the second rung has code 3 versus code 1, proving disjointness. A time-three site's radius-three ball either matches the middle or the corresponding end site of the seven-rung graph when n≥7: neighbors outside that ball cannot enter the three-step dependency cone. If an upper target had both rail neighbors excited at time three, the two upper triggers would give conflicting upper states at column j+2 (1 versus 0 or 2). A rail neighbor and the rung neighbor would give conflicting upper states at column j (0 or 2 versus 1). Reflect across the rails for lower targets. Thus E_4 is empty, E_3 survives as refractory at time four, and tau=5 iff a trigger exists; all-rest is absorbing. Any word in a central dependency window can be embedded for sharpness at every larger length. Prefix counts by depth 0–7 are 1,5,6,12,36,72,72,216, yielding the stated 204 proper-prefix states. Longest-prefix-suffix avoidance transitions count exactly the complement, and independent inclusion–exclusion over windows gives 216,3888,52488,629856 at lengths 7–10. A top word has window probability 108/9^7=4/3^11, proving the stated lower bound using independent disjoint windows. Replay: python3 /workspace/evidence/5_ladder.py (NumPy); output /workspace/evidence/5_ladder.txt. Inspected the frozen C++, Python and output; did not execute uploaded scripts. The finite replay certifies the local cone and small maxima, not an extrapolation from sampled large ladders.

value.rationale: Eventual extinction was previously accessible from sparsity, but it does not answer whether a longer strip can sustain a longer transient. The common smallest strip width with two-contact activation along both axes yields a sharp size-independent cutoff here. The full local classification, rather than only a late witness, decides which initial data attain the cutoff and gives an exact census and a probability law for labelled random states. Both the locality horizon and the count are useful to researchers comparing transient lifetimes across strip widths.
